issues.title: Single underscore include guard used
issues.description: The rule requires header files to use include guards with double underscores at the start (e.g., __FILENAME_H), but the code uses a single underscore prefix instead (_REDIS_H)
issues.rule_name: Header Files Must Use Double-Underscore Include Guards

issues.title: Unsigned integer wraparound in AOF corruption size check
issues.description: The size comparison casts both operands to size_t (unsigned), which causes undefined behavior when valid_up_to exceeds sb.st_size. In this edge case, the subtraction sb.st_size - valid_up_to produces a negative value that wraps around to a very large unsigned integer, always exceeding aof_load_broken_max_size. This prevents automatic recovery even when the corruption is actually small, causing the server to fail to start when it should recover successfully.

issues.title: Incorrect early exit prevents loading incremental AOF after successful base recovery
issues.description: The error handling condition incorrectly treats AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED as a failure state, causing the function to exit immediately after successfully recovering a corrupted base AOF file. When a base AOF is the last file and gets successfully recovered (ret == AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED), the server should continue to load any incremental AOF files. However, this bug causes an early exit to cleanup, preventing incremental files from being loaded and potentially losing data. The correct behavior is to only exit on AOF_OPEN_ERR or AOF_FAILED, not on successful recovery.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #14058 - Add auto-repair options for broken AOF tail on startup

structured_output.summary:
This PR adds two startup options, `aof-load-broken` (default `no`) and `aof-load-broken-max-size` (default 4096 bytes). When an AOF replay hits a format error, Redis can truncate the file back to the last well-formed command and keep loading, but only if the discarded tail is smaller than the limit. The plumbing (config entries, a new `AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED` return code, `valid_up_to` tracking gated behind the option) follows existing `aof-load-truncated` conventions, and the feature is off by default.

The implementation has a serious correctness problem. `valid_up_to` is initialised to 0 and never advanced past an RDB preamble, so for a small RDB-preamble AOF (the default, `aof-use-rdb-preamble yes`) a corrupt tail causes `truncate(file, 0)`, which erases the base data on disk. Two further issues: a non-last file is truncated before the "not last file" fatal check runs, and a recovered last base file skips the size bookkeeping that every other successful load performs. The new tests also do not exercise what their names claim: one assertion matches on any single pattern, and a `rm` call that was meant to delete files is a no-op. I recommend changes before merge.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The RDB-preamble path can silently delete a small base AOF on startup, which is data loss in the feature's core path and is not covered by any test. The non-last-file truncation is destructive before the server refuses to start. Both need fixing before this is safe to enable. The remaining items (size bookkeeping, weak and no-op test steps, an unrelated header-guard rename, doc wording) are smaller but should be addressed in the same pass.

architecture.overview:
At startup, `loadDataFromDisk()` in `src/server.c` calls `loadAppendOnlyFiles()` in `src/aof.c`, which replays the base file and then each incr file through `loadSingleAppendOnlyFile()`. Each replay returns an `AOF_*` code: success, clean EOF, short read (handled by `aof-load-truncated` at the `uxeof` label), or a format error (the `fmterr` label). Before this PR, a format error always returned `AOF_FAILED` and the server exited. Only a short read at the very end could be truncated and recovered.

This PR adds an `aof-load-broken` branch to `fmterr`. It records `valid_up_to` (the file offset after the last well-formed command) and, if the bytes from there to EOF are below `aof-load-broken-max-size`, truncates the file and returns the new `AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED` code. The caller then treats that code like `AOF_TRUNCATED`: it is allowed only on the last file, and anything earlier becomes a fatal error. The RDB-preamble path does not set `valid_up_to`, so the offset is still 0 when the file has a preamble and the first command is malformed.
steps: Entry point: `loadDataFromDisk()` (src/server.c ~7033) calls `loadAppendOnlyFiles()`, which exits only on `AOF_FAILED` or `AOF_OPEN_ERR`.

Replay: `loadSingleAppendOnlyFile()` (src/aof.c ~1483) reads an optional RDB preamble, then parses commands. `valid_up_to` is set after each command only when `aof-load-truncated` or the new `aof-load-broken` is on. The RDB branch never sets it.

New recovery branch: the `fmterr` label (src/aof.c ~1721) truncates the file to `valid_up_to` when the broken tail is under `aof-load-broken-max-size`, then jumps to `loaded_ok` with `AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED`. The truncation happens before the caller knows whether this file is the last one.

Caller policy: `loadAppendOnlyFiles()` (src/aof.c ~1773) allows `AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED` only on the last file. The base-file branch jumps straight to `cleanup` on that code, skipping the `aof_current_size` / `aof_rewrite_base_size` updates. `stopLoading()` and `DEBUG LOADAOF` do not count the new code as success.

Configuration: `aof-load-broken` (bool, default 0) and `aof-load-broken-max-size` (off_t, default 4096) are registered in src/config.c and documented in redis.conf (~lines 1532-1549). The new fields are in src/server.h.

findings.title: RDB-preamble AOF can be truncated to zero bytes, wiping the base data
findings.fixPrompt: In src/aof.c, `loadSingleAppendOnlyFile()` never sets `valid_up_to` after the RDB preamble loads (around lines 1539-1553), so it stays 0. In the `fmterr` recovery branch (around lines 1725-1728), `truncate(aof_filepath, valid_up_to)` then empties a small RDB-preamble base file. After the preamble's `rdbLoadRio()` succeeds, set `valid_up_to = ftello(fp)`. Apply the same fix to the `uxeof` truncation path (around line 1694), which has the same pre-existing bug under `aof-load-truncated`. Add a regression test in tests/integration/aof.tcl: a small RDB-preamble base (`aof-use-rdb-preamble yes`) followed by a garbage line, with `aof-load-broken yes`. Restart and assert that the preamble's keys survive and the file is not truncated to zero.

findings.title: Non-last AOF is truncated before the fatal "not last file" check
findings.body:
`loadSingleAppendOnlyFile()` truncates the file in `fmterr` (line 1728) without knowing whether it is the last file. The check that makes a non-last recovery fatal happens later, in `loadAppendOnlyFiles()` (lines 1836-1839 and 1870-1873). So when a middle segment has a small corrupt tail, the file is cut and the server then exits with "Fatal error: the truncated file is not the last file". Every later command in that file is lost, and the next startup sees the shortened file as if it were healthy.

::diff{file="src/aof.c" lines="1836-1839"}

The log is also misleading: it prints "AOF loaded anyway" (line 1739) for a file that is then rejected. The new test at tests/integration/aof.tcl lines 817-829 passes only because the earlier failed start already truncated `mid`. Its restart is then given an already-repaired file.

Fix: do not truncate inside `loadSingleAppendOnlyFile()`. Return `AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED` with the offset recorded, and let `loadAppendOnlyFiles()` truncate only when the file is the last one. Alternatively, pass a `last_file` flag into the loader.
findings.fixPrompt: In src/aof.c, the `fmterr` recovery branch (around lines 1724-1745) calls `truncate()` before knowing whether the file is the last in the manifest. A non-last file is then truncated and the server exits with "Fatal error: the truncated file is not the last file" (lines ~1836-1839 and ~1870-1873). Change the flow so the file is truncated only after the last-file decision. Either return the recovery offset and let `loadAppendOnlyFiles()` truncate when `last_file` is true, or pass `last_file` into `loadSingleAppendOnlyFile()`. Also fix the "AOF loaded anyway" log, which should not print for a file that will be rejected. Update the intermediate-file test in tests/integration/aof.tcl (around lines 817-829) so it asserts the mid-file bytes are untouched after the failed start.

findings.title: Recovered last base file skips size bookkeeping
findings.body:
`loadAppendOnlyFiles()` jumps to `cleanup` for `AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED` (line 1841) and does so for the base file too. When the recovered base is the last file, the success path never runs `server.aof_current_size = total_size` (line 1881) or `server.aof_rewrite_base_size = base_size` (line 1891). `AOF_TRUNCATED` avoids this because it is not in that early-exit condition.

As a result, after a successful recovery of a base-only AOF, `INFO` reports `aof_current_size:0` and `aof_base_size:0`. The auto-rewrite trigger at src/server.c ~1586-1590 reads both values, so growth-based rewrites are miscalculated until the next rewrite. None of the new tests exercise this path, because the base is never the last file at recovery time.
findings.fixPrompt: In src/aof.c `loadAppendOnlyFiles()`, the base-file branch (around lines 1841-1843) jumps to `cleanup` on `AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED`. That skips the `server.aof_current_size = total_size` and `server.aof_rewrite_base_size = base_size` assignments (around lines 1881 and 1891). Change the early-exit condition so only `AOF_OPEN_ERR` and `AOF_FAILED` jump to `cleanup`, matching how `AOF_TRUNCATED` is handled. A recovered last base file should then take the same bookkeeping path as a clean load. Add a test that recovers a base-only AOF and checks `INFO persistence` reports the loaded size.

findings.title: Test claims last-file base recovery but never exercises it, and its `rm` is a no-op
findings.body:
The block labelled "Corrupted base AOF (last file): should recover" (tests/integration/aof.tcl lines 706-730) does not test what it says:

1. The first `start_server_aof_ex` (line 714) runs with the base file as a non-last file. The recovery truncates the base and then fatals (see the high finding above), so the base has already been repaired on disk.
2. `exec rm -f $aof_dirpath/appendonly.aof.*` (line 724) deletes nothing. Tcl's `exec` does not glob-expand arguments, so `rm` receives the literal pattern and matches no file. The intent was clearly to delete the incr file to make the base last, so the test is not doing what its author expected.
3. The `param == ok` assertion passes on the already-repaired base, so it does not show that the last-file recovery path works.

As written, the test passes whether or not last-file recovery works, which is false confidence. The base-last recovery path (which has the size-bookkeeping bug above) is effectively untested.
findings.fixPrompt: In tests/integration/aof.tcl, the block labelled "Corrupted base AOF (last file): should recover" (around lines 706-730) does not test base-last recovery. The first start (around line 714) makes the base non-last and truncates it. `exec rm -f $aof_dirpath/appendonly.aof.*` (around line 724) is a no-op because Tcl `exec` does not glob. Rewrite it so the base file is the only file in the manifest, or delete the incr file explicitly with `file delete` (or `file rm`) on its path. Then create a corrupt base with a valid `set param ok` prefix and a short garbage tail, start with `aof-load-broken yes`, and assert that `param` is `ok` and the garbage is gone from the file.

findings.title: "Log should mention truncated file is not last" passes on a single pattern
findings.fixPrompt: In tests/integration/aof.tcl, the test "Log should mention truncated file is not last" (around lines 715-719) passes `wait_for_log_messages` two patterns. That helper returns when any one pattern matches, so the "Fatal error: the truncated file is not the last file" check is never really verified. Replace it with separate `wait_for_log_messages` calls, one per pattern, or add a check that the server process exited with an error. Keep the pattern list consistent with the log strings in src/aof.c.

findings.title: AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED missing from success checks in stopLoading and DEBUG LOADAOF
findings.body:
`loadAppendOnlyFiles()` calls `stopLoading(ret == AOF_OK || ret == AOF_TRUNCATED)` (src/aof.c line 1894). For a successful broken-tail recovery, this passes 0. `stopLoading()` then fires `REDISMODULE_SUBEVENT_LOADING_FAILED` on the module event bus, even though the dataset was loaded.

The same omission is in `DEBUG LOADAOF` (src/debug.c around line 600), which returns "Error trying to load the AOF files" when `ret` is `AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED`. The database was loaded, so the reply is wrong.

Both checks should accept `AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED` the same way they accept `AOF_TRUNCATED`.
findings.fixPrompt: Both success predicates need to accept the new recovery code. In src/aof.c `loadAppendOnlyFiles()`, the `stopLoading(...)` call near the end (around line 1894) only treats `AOF_OK` and `AOF_TRUNCATED` as success. Add `AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED`. In src/debug.c around line 600, the `DEBUG LOADAOF` check `ret != AOF_OK && ret != AOF_EMPTY` should also accept `AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED`. Add a module-event or DEBUG LOADAOF test if one is practical.

findings.title: Unrelated header-guard rename in server.h
findings.body:
The PR changes `#ifndef __REDIS_H` to `#ifndef _REDIS_H` (src/server.h lines 15-16). That change has nothing to do with AOF recovery. Identifiers that begin with an underscore followed by an uppercase letter are reserved for the implementation, so `_REDIS_H` is a worse choice than the original `__REDIS_H`, which is also reserved. The rename is harmless to the build, but it adds noise to an otherwise focused diff and should be dropped.

::diff{file="src/server.h" lines="15-16"}
findings.fixPrompt: In src/server.h, revert the unrelated include-guard change so the guard matches the original (around lines 15-16). Keep this PR limited to the AOF recovery feature.

findings.title: redis.conf describes the feature as handling corruption "in the middle"
findings.fixPrompt: In redis.conf, the new `aof-load-broken` comment block (around lines 1532-1547) says the feature applies "when the AOF file is corrupted in the middle". Correct it to say that recovery discards everything from the first malformed command to the end of the file, including valid commands after it, and that `aof-load-broken-max-size` is measured from that first bad byte. Keep the existing warning about data loss.

findings.title: Too-large tail skips the redis-check-aof hint
findings.body: When the broken tail is over `aof-load-broken-max-size`, the `fmterr` branch logs only that the size limit was exceeded (src/aof.c lines 1746-1752). The `else` branch, used when `aof-load-broken` is off, prints the `redis-check-aof --fix` guidance. The option's documentation promises that the operator will be told to run `redis-check-aof` in this case, but the message does not say so. An operator facing a rejected file gets less guidance than before the PR.
findings.fixPrompt: In src/aof.c `fmterr`, the branch where the broken tail exceeds `aof-load-broken-max-size` (around lines 1746-1752) should also tell the operator to run `./redis-check-aof --fix <filename.manifest>`, as the `else` branch does. Reuse the same wording so the guidance is consistent. The redis.conf comment says the server will require manual intervention with `redis-check-aof` in this case.

findings.title: Config plumbing and defaults follow existing patterns
findings.body: The new options are registered the same way as `aof-load-truncated`. `aof-load-broken` defaults to `no`, so existing deployments see no change. The size limit defaults to 4096, which matches `redis.conf`, and it has a lower bound of 0. The `valid_up_to` tracking is gated behind the option, so the common path does not pay for it. The reserved-looking `__REDIS_H` rename aside, the header additions are minimal.

findings.title: Good test coverage for the size-limit and mid-chain paths
findings.body: The tests cover three useful cases: a tail under the limit being recovered, a tail over a 2-byte limit being rejected (the "Bad format" test around line 787), and a corrupt non-last incr file failing fatally (line 818). These are the right scenarios to test for the size boundary and the multi-file rule. The gaps are the RDB-preamble case and the base-last bookkeeping, which the findings above describe.
